title: Operator Administration Without SQL
objective: Authorized Oxford Lancers administrators can provision and manage application operators and their predefined role assignments through the application without requiring Brian to run SQL or make ordinary account changes directly in Supabase, including onboarding every fixed coaching role with the approved bounded attendance and availability capabilities.
why_now: The authorization substrate, login and password recovery exist, but the hosted role catalogue and recurring operator-administration workflow are not available through the application. The approved Release 1 manifest marks Identity, Access and Operator Administration ready for intake, while current operation still depends on direct database changes.
non_goals: No runtime creation, renaming or editing of club roles or capability grants; the approved static 20-role catalogue includes the fixed coaching hierarchy
No wider H7 ownership and access completion sweep
No LAN-84 production recovery rehearsal or two-service-administrator establishment
No Meta, WhatsApp, DNS, broader Resend/SMTP email-foundation or real-data cutover work; this mission may consume the owner-provided Resend API key for first-access delivery only
No player-facing accounts, persona-specific duplicate logins or public sign-up
No authentication-architecture redesign or operator two-factor authentication
No general People/roster redesign, operator self-service profile editing or player-facing authentication beyond duplicate-checked create-or-link Person needed for operator invitation

No coach module, football-assignment/depth-chart self-service, injury or medical narrative, general roster/contact visibility, availability history/actor identity or unapproved coach capability grants; this mission includes onboarding all fixed coaching roles with approved narrow attendance and current availability Orange/Red reporting only
No special bulk handover mode or general cycle-open/close implementation
No full Stage-4 general change-audit browser, cross-system search, filtering, export or investigation interface; bounded Operator audit history and Holder history projections are included
No Mission Lead DAG, worker assignment, detailed work package or implementation sequencing in this packet
No mission execution before Brian merges a ready packet version

requirements.text: The application uses the approved static 20-role catalogue: Operational Administration—General Manager and IT Officer; Club Committee—President, Vice-President, Secretary, Treasurer, Social Secretary, Gameday Secretary, Kit Manager and Media Secretary; Coaching Staff—Head Coach, Offensive Coordinator, Defensive Coordinator, Quarterbacks Coach, Offensive Line Coach, Wide Receivers Coach, Defensive Line Coach, Linebackers Coach, Defensive Backs Coach and Special Teams Coach. The catalogue appears in that group order, is available in hosted and local environments through versioned reviewable repository artifacts, and cannot be edited in the application.

Every operator-administration read and write is enforced at the server/service boundary by role_management plus target-level leadership and recovery guards. President, General Manager and IT Officer hold role_management. Vice-President and Secretary retain broad ordinary operating capabilities but cannot administer accounts or role assignments. General Manager may manage President; IT Officer may recover leadership email access but may not ordinarily assign, replace, end or deactivate President or General Manager.

The operator shell contains Operators and Roles at /operate/admin/operators and /operate/admin/roles in Administration at the bottom of the left sidebar above user/account controls. Invite Operator is the top-right primary action. The protected /operate/admin/guide page is reached from a compact question-mark How Administration Works link beside the page heading, not a callout or another sidebar destination. Operators are grouped Standing Officers, Club Officers and Coaches; Roles are grouped Operational Administration, Club Committee and Coaching Staff. Role detail presents current holder, a plain-language Permissions summary and holder history. Operator detail uses club-facing labels and distinguishes operator account state from role state. No role or grant is editable.

The checked-in self-contained Administration prototype is the controlling visual reference for the reviewed information architecture, grouping, labels, actions, account and invitation states, FAQ guide structure, and desktop/375px responsive direction. Its synthetic names, dates, counts, exact spacing, border shades and low-level component composition are illustrative. Implementation uses the existing Material UI shell and must not infer authorization, data behavior or additional scope from prototype-only sample content.

An authorized administrator first searches and duplicate-checks for the durable Person. If found, including a current or former player, the workflow links that Person; if absent, it creates a minimal Person with required first name, last name and valid personal email plus optional phone number. The same guided flow requires at least one approved initial role, inherits the active operating year, defaults effective-from to today with permitted future/backdating, creates at most one operator login, and emails a secure invitation. Public sign-up remains disabled, and profile editing is deferred to a later mission.

The workflow represents Invitation pending, Delivery failed, Active, Deactivated and Email change pending states with distinct text and visual treatment; reinstatement returns the same operator to Active. It records invitation send/delivery attempts, treats expiration as normal, exposes resend while pending or failed, permits correction and resend, and refuses duplicate Person bindings or duplicate emails with an actionable reason. Delivery failure preserves the same Person and operator account and never creates a duplicate.

The first version inherits one application-wide active operating-year context for routine assignments. Forms do not ask for or repeat the year and stored cycle remains explicit. Current year is writable; past years require deliberate switching and are read-only. This mission does not create or close years. A future year is unavailable until lifecycle creates it; once open, authorized administrators may deliberately switch and prepare assignments under the same guards. Holders from different years are never mixed.

Ordinary roles inherit the active operating year and an effective-from date defaulting to today; future dates and audited backdating are permitted. No routine end date is requested. End assignment may schedule a future effective-to and requires a reason; replacement ends the outgoing assignment and creates the successor without rewriting history. General Manager is standing and single-holder; IT Officer is also standing; neither expires automatically at year end.

An authorized administrator can immediately Deactivate operator access with a required reason and Restore operator access on the same Person-account binding later. Deactivation prevents sign-in without ending organizational roles, making a role pending or creating a vacancy; role detail instead shows that the current holder's operator access is deactivated. Reinstatement restores only capabilities from assignments that remain effective. Replace role ends the outgoing assignment and creates the successor, who may remain Invitation pending without capabilities until activation. Only explicit End role creates a Not assigned vacancy. No action deletes Person, membership, binding, attribution or history.

Forgotten password remains self-service through verified email. For lost or compromised email, an authorized administrator disables the old login path, records a reason, sends a secure verification link to an unused replacement email and keeps the account in Email change pending until verification. Failure is correctable and retryable on the same account. General Manager may recover President; IT Officer may technically recover President or General Manager without changing their authority; President may not recover General Manager.

No operator may deactivate themselves, end/remove their own role assignment or use the administrator recovery flow on themselves. General Manager may assign, replace, end or deactivate President; President and IT Officer may not ordinarily assign, replace, end or deactivate General Manager; IT Officer may not ordinarily assign, replace, end or deactivate President. President, General Manager and IT Officer may administer lower roles. No action may eliminate every usable administration path; General Manager replacement remains exceptional IT/service recovery outside this mission.

Every provisioning, account-state, email-recovery and role-assignment change writes one append-only canonical audit event naming actor, authority at the time, target Person/operator, affected role/assignment when applicable, operating year, timestamp, reason and before/after state. Operator audit history shows target-affecting events; role detail shows the role-related subset as Holder history. The same event may appear in both projections without duplicate records. Ordinary page views and refused no-change actions are excluded; the full Stage-4 general audit browser remains excluded.

Implementation delivers one versioned idempotent database migration for the approved 20-role catalogue and mission-owned schema/constraints, plus one supported idempotent owner-run bootstrap script using the Supabase administrative API rather than direct SQL insertion into Auth-owned tables. The bootstrap dry-runs and duplicate-checks existing Person/operator/auth state, then establishes at least Clint as active-year President, Stewart as standing General Manager and Brian as standing IT Officer from owner-supplied exact names/emails, with audit evidence and fail-closed conflict handling. Brian reviews and performs or explicitly directs production execution. After verification, any later manual SQL provisioning touch is a defect.

A protected in-app guide at /operate/admin/guide, linked from Operators and Roles through the compact How Administration Works question-mark link, uses FAQ-style expandable questions for inviting someone, assigning/replacing/ending a role, deactivating/restoring access, resending an invitation and recovering email access. It also explains combined player/operator/role identity, active/past/future year behavior, hierarchy, audit projections, refusals and escalation. It contains no callouts, SQL, Supabase-dashboard, administrator-created-password or WhatsApp-authentication procedure.

Implementation and verification do not alter hosted accounts, production data, secrets, email/DNS configuration or recovery ownership autonomously. Any migration or one-time hosted bootstrap remains an explicit Brian-run handoff under existing runbooks.

President, General Manager and IT Officer may assign people to the approved static catalogue, including roles that currently carry no privileged capabilities. Single-holder restrictions follow the constitution, with General Manager additionally single-holder; other roles permit multiple holders unless another authoritative rule says otherwise. One Person may hold multiple compatible roles. Administrators cannot create roles or edit grants in the application.

Administration visually separates Coaching Staff and supports duplicate-checked create-or-link Person, secure email invitation and active-year role assignment for all ten fixed coaching roles. Coaching onboarding neither requires nor automatically creates player membership: an external coach may have none, while a coach-player links the existing Person and membership. One Person and at most one operator login may simultaneously carry player membership and compatible committee, operational and coaching roles. Every fixed coaching role receives only the approved narrow attendance capability, including minimal walk-up capture, plus current availability viewing and Orange/Red reporting. Coaches cannot confirm Green, see availability history or actor identity, see injury/medical narrative or general roster/contact data, or use football-assignment/depth-chart self-service.

The only new informational email is first-time access invitation and resend. Password reset and replacement-email verification/security messages remain functional security mechanisms; role assignment/end/replacement, deactivation and reinstatement send no informational emails. Supabase Auth uses the available Resend-backed transactional path. Brian supplies the API key through an approved secure owner-gated environment path; secrets never appear in source, SQL, Notion, packet, logs or client code. Real production first-access delivery is required for acceptance, while broader Resend account/DNS/LAN-126 work remains excluded.

Role and coach capability explanations shown in Administration are derived from the same reviewed capability definition used by server enforcement, so a later approved grant change updates authorization and plain-language UI copy together rather than leaving stale duplicated descriptions.
